title: 17th Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The 17th sitting of the third session opened on 10 November 2025 at 09:02 and closed at 11:13. After routine business, four members spoke in the opening debate on the 2026 state budget (MVR 64.2 billion), with supporters pointing to falling deficits and local projects and the opposition member questioning debt, pay changes and unkept promises; the chair then paused the debate because no more members wished to speak, saying it would resume on Wednesday and the following Sunday. The Evidence Act amendment bill was accepted for study and sent to the Judiciary Committee, and the Trademarks Bill and the Judges Act amendment bill both passed, all by votes of 63 to 64 in favour with none against. The text has some garbled digits, so the attendance count at the start is as read from the text.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Called the budget hopeful, citing debt reduction targets, health and education spending, and the judiciary's financial independence; asked for funding for Huraa and Hinmafushi projects.
On the Judges Act bill, backed requiring judges to hold qualifications in Islamic Shari'ah and law.

speakers.name: Adam Shafeeq
positions: Backed the 2026 budget as fulfilling the President's pledges, citing rising revenue, a falling deficit and progress on projects in his constituency.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Reviewed the budget's revenue, spending and debt figures and welcomed its direction.
Asked that pay harmonisation for staff follow one common principle.
Supported a customs container scanner to curb revenue leakage.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Criticised the budget as unclear on delivery, citing rising national debt, Aasandha costs, civil service pay concerns and unkept promises for Hanimaadhoo.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Presented the Economic Committee report on the Trademarks Bill, noting consultation with agencies and several amendments to align it with copyright law.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: As the bill's sponsor, said the Trademarks Bill protects businesses, supports foreign investment and helps consumers identify genuine goods.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Presented the Judiciary Committee report on the Judges Act amendment, noting consultation with the Judicial Service Commission, courts department, Bar Council and judges' association.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: Spoke on Shari'ah principles of fair trial, urged judges to rule honestly, and said courts have been speeding up and handling corruption cases.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 2025/3/11 to 2025/3/14 were accepted as no amendments were filed.
Committee deadlines announced: Foreign Relations Committee 12 Nov 2025, Economic Committee 20 Nov 2025.
The 2026 budget debate was paused with no more speakers, to continue on Wednesday and the following Sunday.
The Evidence Act amendment bill was accepted for consideration and sent to the Judiciary Committee.
The bill amending the Judges Act (Law 2010/13) was passed.
The next sitting was set for 12 Nov 2025 at 09:00.

votes.what: Accept the Evidence Act amendment bill for consideration (sent to Judiciary Committee)
Pass the bill to amend the Judges Act (Law 2010/13)
